character_facts: Cyber-cops are active on or above Terra 2014 and conduct surveillance of the city-shaft.
The Zacuda Frolex is described as the last of its kind.
characters_present: Cyber-cops/patrol crew, seen indirectly through their vehicle or equipment
continuity_links: This page functions as an establishing opening, setting the state of Terra 2014 before events proceed inside the city-shaft.
The rare Zacuda Frolex being dropped into the hatch appears to initiate a forthcoming event or intrusion into the abandoned city-shaft.
dialogue_meaning: The narration introduces Terra 2014 as a harsh, windswept place with a smooth engineered outer shell.
The city-shaft is under surveillance, but the watch is effectively pointless because it has been uninhabited for centuries.
A rare being or object called a Zacuda Frolex is carried by the wind.
That Zacuda Frolex enters the city-shaft through a ventilation opening.
locations: The smooth Teflo-concrete shell of Terra 2014
A ventilation hatch in the shell
lore_facts: Terra 2014 has a smooth outer shell made of Teflo-concrete.
Strong winds sweep across the shell of Terra 2014.
The city-shaft has been uninhabited by humans for over three centuries.
A 'Zacuda Frolex' exists and is identified here as the last of its kind.
The shell includes ventilation hatches that open into the structure below.
plot_events: An aerial patrol craft moves over the outer shell of Terra 2014.
Narration establishes that cyber-cops are watching the city-shaft, but no humans have lived there for more than three centuries.
A wind gust carries a Zacuda Frolex identified as the last of its kind.
The object is dropped through one of the shell's ventilation hatches.
uncertainties: The exact visual form of the Zacuda Frolex is small and indistinct in the panel; it may be a creature, object, or container, but the page does not make this fully clear visually.
No individual cyber-cop is clearly visible or identifiable by name on this page.
visual_summary: A large aircraft or patrol craft crosses a vast pale surface under a pink sky above the curved shell of Terra 2014. The page then looks down through or across the craft toward a huge circular city-shaft opening. Later panels show debris or a windblown object moving through the air and being dropped through a ventilation hatch on the shell.
